title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 125.858271: one address rule for both parities and a shorter plain fused pass 1, on shared-row pass 2

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack of proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^125.858271 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). It builds on bradcush's a00774d8 (125.862153: c06f6691 with pass 2's products by R on shared rows), whose walk, census, kappa, pass 2 and meter it keeps, with one change to the arrival: the odd-y half of each table row is stored permuted (row rho holds -Tab[(P' - rho) mod 2^25][j], P' = 0x1fffe17), so every arrival path (pass1f, pass1p, arrive.s) inserts bits 0..25 of y0 into the address on both parities and the class walk is unchanged (for odd y, y0 = p0 - K0 mod 2^26 whatever the borrow). The plain rounds' fused pass 1 (one key test per parity, one STP per pair, loop count in x0) is 125.515625 instructions per walk instead of 127.03125: step 125.515625 + 432.515625 + 25616/2^20 = 558.0556. pass1f keeps 129.03125, so compare rounds cost 3.515625 per walk (a hard row). The declared run executes both fused copies (0 mismatches against the new address rule, odd borrows injected), arrive.s, the loops and all 1,554 exit stubs. kappa = 1.0001 follows from the shipped hazard census as in c06f6691. Declared dependencies (proof.md section 6): a00774d8, c06f6691, 4ac17b66, 445f9a1c, cbea87bf, 4c8222cc, 673640ef, 0a1c5772, 610c8e49, 6a6cb91c, 5f1ae3ce, 4595bad7, 01488655, 2bd168b5, daf2c741, 4b4defe7, a9297fb0, 807e4bf5, b5de673a, 02feb284. Recovery probability is greater than 0.39000019 and therefore at least 0.39 (failure rows 1.0103e-7 < 1.1e-7). Peak memory < 2^72 bytes; preprocessing capped at 2^59 units and included; no advice. Exact ledger: S_ops = 1.0001*S0 = 2^126.6995433, phase 1 = 2^125.858024, hard extras = 2^111.798320, random extras = 2^98.8271, allowance = 2^112.7362, W_ledger = 2^125.8582706 <= 1000*2^125.858271 milli-units; Markov ratio 0.0000648320 < 0.000065; certificate.py checks the claim and that 125.858270 fails, in exact arithmetic. No prior acceptance, review verdict or official score is a premise. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and the canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled toy pipeline of the checkpoint-only walk (even-y key, per-trail phases, compares every 128th round) on subgroups of y^2=x^3+7 with node routing, a check that the old and the production compare rule reach the same endpoints, and a long-trail trap test; kernels: Python limb ports of the field kernels against big integers, and the shipped loops (with rare exits on constructed inputs entering every stub), both copies of the fused pass 1, emitter wrappers and arrival rows executed by an AArch64 interpreter (kernels/a64.py) against affine secp256k1, a bit-exact model and the exact canonical rule, with instruction counts and the ledger recomputed. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
